lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: CHAPTER 27
lines.note: Chapter heading.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The Man Who Refused
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They did not return to the plaza.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The knocking faded after a time, as if the City had noted their refusal and simply transferred the account to a later column. The three paving stones looked ordinary again. Only the erased names on the lintels remained as proof that someone had once answered when asked.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg kept his hand on Zeek's shoulder until they were well clear of the unfinished street.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Next time you test a threshold,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: he said,
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: you say so first.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek nodded. He still tasted the shape of his own full name at the back of his throat.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-KHEH-doo glanced back once at the blank floor.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: We still don't know what happens if someone actually pays.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: We know enough,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon answered. She was writing again, stylus moving in short, precise strokes.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: That distinction survives in every damaged tablet that still mentions the gates.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They chose a narrower street that at least possessed two walls and a visible far end. The geometry continued to refuse ordinary rules. A covered walkway they passed beneath reappeared ahead of them a short while later, identical down to one cracked tile. Zeek stopped leaving trail markers. There was no longer any point.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The deeper they went, the more traces of ordinary life surfaced—and the more wrong those traces felt. A market stall carved directly into a building's side still held the faint outlines of jars that no longer existed. A child's handprint was pressed into a wall at waist height, the fingers too small, the impression too deep. Doorways showed thresholds worn smooth by generations of feet, yet their upper lintels remained sharp, as if the people who lived here had eventually stopped looking up.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon slowed beside a low wall covered in faint wedge-shaped marks. She brushed dust away with careful fingers.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Inventory,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Grain. Oil. Rope. The same lists every household kept.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Near the bottom three lines had been crossed out so thoroughly the surface beneath was scraped raw. Beside the erasure someone had later cut a single incomplete spiral.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: They inventoried people,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: she said quietly.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: No one asked her to continue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The street narrowed further. Torchlight sank into the oily stone and did not return. Somewhere ahead, water dripped with the slow regularity of a clock that no longer measured hours anyone recognized.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then they heard the voice.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It was thin, human, and exhausted, and it came from a side passage so narrow they would have walked past it without noticing.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: Don't give it your name.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg's axe was up before the last word finished. En-KHEH-doo had already angled herself for a fight. NEEN-soon froze with the stylus still pressed to parchment.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek raised the torch.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The passage ended after only a few paces in a shallow alcove. A man sat against the back wall, knees drawn up, wrists resting loosely on them. His clothes were the same dust-fused linen they had seen on the gatekeeper, but his skin was still skin—gray, stretched thin, cracked at the corners of the mouth. His eyes tracked the torchlight with the slow recognition of someone who had not expected living faces again.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: You're real,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: the man said. His voice sounded unused.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: I thought the City had finally learned how to make better copies.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek crouched just out of reach.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: Who are you?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The man gave a one-sided smile.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: That depends which name you're asking for. The one I arrived with, or the one it left me.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon's stylus hovered.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: How long have you been here?

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: I stopped counting after the second winter that never ended.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He looked past them toward the main street.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: You're still carrying your names. That's rarer than it should be. Most who reach this depth have already paid at least once.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg kept the axe ready.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Are there others?

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: There were.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The man lifted one thin hand and pointed farther down the narrowing street.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: The City keeps what it collects. Sometimes it lets the emptier ones walk for a while. Sometimes it uses them as markers. Sometimes it just leaves them where they fall.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-KHEH-doo studied him the way she studied anything that might still hold value.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Enhedu
lines.text: What did you pay?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The man's gaze settled on BAH-lahg.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: The first threshold accepted your offering,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: he said. Then, to Zeek:
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: First took a knife I inherited. Ordinary steel. Second took a scar I earned above. Third asked for the name of the woman who waited for me. She used to—

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He stopped. His mouth worked around a word that would not come.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: I can still see her face,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: he said at last.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: I just can't remember what anyone ever called her.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Silence settled over the alcove.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon spoke carefully.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: And the fourth?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The man looked at Zeek's wrapped hand, at the journal, at the mark that still pulsed faintly beneath the linen.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: The fourth is why I'm still sitting here. I refused. The City does not force the later payments. It waits. And while it waits, the streets rearrange. The people you arrived with begin to forget why they came. Eventually you forget too—or you decide that whatever is left of you is still too expensive to keep.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He leaned his head back against the stone.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: You're marked,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: he said to Zeek.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: That means an account is already open. Everything after this is collection.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The journal pressed once against Zeek's ribs—deliberate, almost like confirmation.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The man closed his eyes.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: Don't give it your name. And if you reach the place where the walls begin to breathe in time with your pulse, turn around. That threshold does not ask. It only records the answer you already gave by arriving.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg lowered the axe and offered his hand.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Balag
lines.text: Come with us.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The man stared at the open hand for a long time.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: I have followed strangers out of this alcove before,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: he said.
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: The Man Who Refused
lines.text: They always bring me back.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He did not take the hand.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They left him there.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: As they moved back into the main street, NEEN-soon spoke almost to herself.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The tablets never mentioned survivors.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Behind them, in the narrow alcove, the man began to hum—soft, tuneless, keeping time with a clock only he could still hear.
